input: Um, could you tell me about the games you used to play when you were a kid? Ooh. We used to play ball. Mm-hm. And sometime we would play, uh, /unintelligible/ have a piece that you'd hide it. So /where I'd / call it, uh, hide the switch. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. And then we would, uh, have a vine and play catch rope. Uh-huh. How do you play that? Catch rope. Well take it this way. Yeah. And then jump rope, and we'd catch- your feet or something catch in it, then it'd whip you with it. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Oh, I see. When you miss jumping. Ooh. Yeah, you'd missed jumped it. They'd take it and hit your legs with it like that. Mm-hm. Did you jump rope? Uh, sometime I could. Uh-huh. And, uh, did you ever have any rhymes you used to jump rope with? Vines? Rhymes. No. You never said any? No. Any kids' rhymes? Uh, let's see. Did you ever play one game where Mm. one person would say, hide his eyes. And- uh, and everybody else would run away and hide? Yeah, they call it hide and seek. Uh-huh. And suppose you were it. What would you have to do? I'd have to run and hide myself. Mm-hm. From the others. Uh-huh. And the person who was coming to look for you would do what? Mm. Would he count to give you enough time? No, he would look somewhere and try to find me. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. And, um, what happened when he found you? He'd run back to the, uh, base. Mm-hm. And if- if you beat him back, were you free? Yeah. And that's /really it/. Yeah. What would you say when you got back there first? If you were in free. Would you shout something, or? Yeah, I'd jump. /?/ I got. /unintelligible/ Okay. Um. Hm. What, uh, What about- uh, about jacks? Did you ever play jacks? No. Did you ever play marbles? N- I- I ain't never played no marbles. What, the men- the boys did that? Yeah, they'd slip and play marbles, some. Excuse me a minute. Let me run and get /inaudible/. /inaudible/. What kinds of marbles would the guys have? Would they have different sorts? Were there names for different shapes and different sizes of 'em? N- no, they'd have a mar- a little marble and wanted to shoot the marble and Mm-hm. then the other on would shoot it. Yeah. Yeah. Uh, did you ever play- uh, did you ever play that game that the kids all play now with chalk on the sidewalk? No, I wouldn't play that. Mm-hm. Scared that I'd fall or something. You'd what? I'd be afraid I'd fall. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh, what would you do with the- with the other girls? I'd probably play hide, and jumping rope, and Mm-hm. things like that. Mm-hm. Uh, do you watch television nowadays? Yeah. I look at- on- on at the television yesterday. Oh yeah? Uh, did you see anything good? I saw a play on there looked pretty nice. Mm-hm. What was it about? Can you tell me? I don't think I can. I saw so many things. Have you seen any good ones lately that you could tell me about? Oh, yeah. I saw that about- um. The man- one of the men was catching fish and the other was- had a son followed him. Mm-hm. And the son had a whistle. He was blowing the whistle and- hm, and it- that little son would run and play with the- what they're trying to catch /him/. Mm-hm. And did he? M- But- No. He didn't catch up with him that time, but The first time he didn't catch /her/. Mm-hm. But the last time, he- he caught up with him. What'd he do? Then they stopped and went on together. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Have- Do you have a pet? Hm? Do you have a pet? No, we haven't got a pet around an- anywhere. Did you- did you ever? have a dog around here. I beg your pardon? /??/ has a little dog around here but, she don't play. She played with him sometime out there in the streets. Do you ever play with him? No. Did you have a dog when you were a kid? Oh, yeah. My father had two dogs. What'd did they do? Hunt. Hunt rabbits. Rabbits? What kind were they? Oh, it was large size rabbits. Hm? It was large-sized rabbits. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. And what sort of dogs were they? Oh they was small dogs. Were they? Were they good at getting the rabbits? Yeah. Did you ever go hunting with them? Or did- No. s- do that. I stayed busy doing other things. Uh-huh. What would you do? Work in the garden. Uh-huh. Things like that. What would you like to do in the garden? I mean, what kinds of things did you grow? Onions. Uh-huh. Tomatoes. Mm-hm. Beets. Were they hard to grow? No. Just a lot of work in there weeding /everything/. That's all j- j- just a lot of work. When you were a kid was there any way that you were supposed to be able to get a wish? No, sure wasn't. Not often, /course/. Hm? I said, not often. No way. Yeah. Yeah. Was there any way that you were supposed to be able to? I mean, did you ever use the bone of a chicken, or anything like that? Oh, I know what you're talking about a bone. They call it a wishbone. Uh-huh. No, I never did play that. Mm-hm. What would you- what would you do when a tooth came out? Did they make the fuss they do nowadays? Would you put it under your pillow? A tooth? Yeah. When you were a little kid and your- all your baby teeth /came out/. No. I'd throw all that- throw- throw 'em away quick as they'd come out. Oh, yeah? Tell me about your school. When you were a little girl, what did you do? Did you e- did you go to school? Yeah, I went to school alright enough. Part of the time. Mm-hm. I was wondering. Were- did you live on a farm? Mm-hm. Yeah, my father had a l- a large farm. Is- So you'd, what? Go to school to the morning and come back and work in the afternoon, or would you go the whole day, or what? I'd go the whole day. After father done laid the crop around, then we could go on to school. /Right/ Hm? After my father done laid the crop by, we'd go to- Mm-hm. go to school then. So would you stay out when the- uh, when the harvest was around? No, we had to help him. Yeah. Yeah. /Same but/ my father was raised on a farm in Missouri. Where was your farm? Mm. Mm-hm. Gibbs, Louisiana. In Louisiana? Mm-hm. What did you g- what did you raise? What did you grow? Cotton and anything you could think of. What was your class like? Hm? What was your classroom like? Hm. It's a large room. Mm-hm. Where did the kids sit? On their desk. Mm-hm. And, um, t- would the teacher write up on? On the wall, I was about to say. Was there any place for her to write with chalk? Yeah, we had blackboards. Mm-hm. Sometime she'd write a word on that. /?/ Trying what? And then she'd have you to spell it. Mm-hm. And she would write it so fast, we couldn't hardly get your words together. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Mm-hm. Did you used to have spelling contests? Yeah, but I couldn't spell them words. /?/ Mm-hm. /unintelligible/ Put 'em on there real quick. Yeah. And, uh, if you could spell those words, you could pass. Mm-hm. But what I liked was, it was printing. Mm-hm. After my eyes got bad, I just stopped trying. Didn't like to. When did that happen to you? Well. been a long years ago. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Did you ever have a teacher who hollered at you a lot? No. Did you ever get yelled at? Sometime they'd holler at us. We'd be out there playing and wouldn't wanna come in the house, and. Uh-huh. But, uh, the teachers nev- you didn't have a teacher that just liked to holler? No. Did. No, back then they had switches. Oh, ho, ho. Did you ever get switched when it wasn't your fault? Yeah, cause I- when I was a kid about the size of them children /down there/, /where you sit where we had/ school sometime, I'd take a- take my finger like that a pop it. Uh-huh. I'd pop somebody. /there/ with it. Uh-huh. And they'd sit there and laugh at it. /?/ What's the- what's the matter w- with ? And then she'd go to crying. Sure enough /?/. /unintelligible/ hit me. Mm-hm. What she hit you with? She popped my head. It was fun to me. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Uh, did- can you tell me about the best teacher you had? Did you have any good teachers? Yeah. What were they like? Who were they? Well, my last teacher was Professor . Mm-hm. Why did they call him professor? G- Well he was a school teacher, /cause he was a printer/. Mm-hm. Were all the men, professor, and all the women, teacher, or? Or wasn't there any distinction like that? Mm-hm. It's on that order. I beg your pardon? I said, it was it was on that order /really/. Yeah. Mm-hm. Would you ever call a man a teacher instead of a professor? Uh, well he was a head teacher and the- and the prof- professor too, you see. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Did the smart kids get any special favors? That the ordinary kids didn't get? Yeah, because, see a lot of kids didn't paying attention much to their lessons and s- some did. Mm-hm. And they would pass, and some wouldn't pass anything. Mm-hm. What about the dumb kids? They'd just get left back? They'd just be left out. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Uh, what time did you go to school in the morning? Nine o'clock. And so you'd have to leave home when? About what time? Mm, about something to eight. Something to eight? Really? Mm-hm. Took you an hour to get to school? No. How far was it? It was a good piece. It sounds like. Was there a bunch of girls you hung around with particularly? No. Uh, was this because it was a rural area, or? What would you do if you could do it all over again, starting now? Would you do anything different? Oh, yeah. Cause I'd try to learn something now. Learn more, you know w- learn how to write. Mm-hm. Well if I didn't learning anything, I'd try to learn, uh- uh, try to learn how to write. Mm-hm. Would you- would you go to school- would you go to college? Or wouldn't you care to? You know, if you started again cold. Cause it's so different now. /True/. I don't know. Do you think things have changed? Well yeah, I sure do. Everything done changed, look like to me. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Uh, /??/. Oh, if I had a chance to go to school Yeah. again- Mm-hm. Say you had a chance to go to school again. I would, uh, try to learn how to write and how to count. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Things like that. Mm-hm. Uh, if you had all the money in the world suddenly dumped in your lap as you sat there, what would you do with it? I don't know. I'd start me a bank. Yes, I do know what I- I wanna. I think I'd start me a bank. Uh-huh. I'd give some things to poor children. Uh-huh. And to orphan children. I'm a printer, and I'd be /true/ glad to stay to that. Again. Would you like to study printing again? Yeah. I love to print signs and Bible quotations. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Course, I could print on anything I could mark on. Really? Yeah. Can you- uh, do you use, what silk screen, or? No, I used letters. What- what kinds of- Letters. So. Alphabets, yeah. Mm-hm. What do you use? Gloss printing, or? Uh, hand printing. Uh-huh. Very good. Mm-hm. /Press/ letters and So. /inaudible/. What tools would you use then? Uh, Brushes, or? yeah. I'd use brushes. Mm-hm. How do you do it? Just pick some kind of paint that will stay on whatever. Yeah. Whatever I printed. Did you do things for the church, or? Oh, yeah. I do things for the church. What church do you belong to? Print Bible quotations and things like that. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. For the Sunday school or on the main And, uh. church, or? Mm. Zion Chapel. Uh-huh. Have you always been a member of that church? No. I used a Baptist. Did you? Mm-hm. When'd you change? When you moved here, or? Mm-hm. Hm. And I was reared up in a Baptist church, and when my father died I moved to Jackson, Mississippi. And then Mm-hm. I stayed around there til I married. Then I come on up here. Mm-hm. Which was? A- around when? How old were you about when you came up here? Who me? Yeah. I couldn't tell you now cause I'm sixty-five, now. Was it i- was it early in the century, or? Mm-hm. Hm, pretty early. Maybe the twenties or something? It was something. No, I- I wasn't in- I wasn't in no twenties, I know. When you came here? No. Oh boy. What do they call this part of town? Little /unintelligible/ Now, when I was a little bit younger, I'd /?/ him back. I shoot right straight back. What is it? That's /sale paper/. /?/ Should I? No, he might say he /?/. He might say he did well to, uh, you did it on purpose or something. Well, I would've. Yeah, have a little fun. I don't know what you can do with sale papers but light a fire. Mm. That's all. Hm. What do they call this part of town? Just Highland Park, or? Yeah. Highland Park. And does- would you ever call this a part of, uh, the city? Or do you see it as being something very much separate? Mm-hm. I see it as part of the city because it's so many cars and- and buses and things runs out here. Mm-hm. And they run straight to downtown, uh. Mm-hm. That's right. And the city's name is? Hm? And the city is? What? We call it Detroit. Call it Detroit? Mm-hm. Uh, And this is Highland Park. Highland Park. Mm-hm. Can you name some of the streets? Hm, I ain't been out here that long. On this part, no way. Mm-hm. We ain't been too long moved out here. Do you know- can you name some of the streets of Detroit? Twenty-Fourth and Twenty- Sixth, over yonder. Mm-hm. What about the big ones? What's the big one a few blocks over yonder? On which side? It comes up and splits the city in east and west? Y- uh. Over the East Side is a street over there. Large street over there. They call it, uh, Charlevoix and Townsend. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. And the big city- and the big street that cuts Detroit east and west is? Buchanan. Okay. Um. Now tell me, what is you gonna do with that? Oh. We don't really know yet. We know a lot of things we're gonna try. We're going to see. What is you gonna try? We're gonna try seeing if there's any relationship between what people do and how they talk. Where they come from and how they talk. See if there's any difference in the way your voice goes up in a question, and they way down the street would. You know, and just see if we can find any kind of patterns to tell us how Detroit people speak. And then from that, we're gonna try to tell the grade school teachers what to teach the kids. Uh, that's nice to do that. Well it's- I don't know. /And also/. To get it started is the thing. You know when- Basically, of course, we're doing it for the Negro children. You know that. For the colored race? Yes. Yeah. You know when this, uh, yes and no come out? A lot of the children took up with it. Mm-hm. A lot of children, what? A lot of children took up with it. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Uh. What would you rather be called? Colored or Negro? Or. Me? Yeah. I like to be called a colored girl. Would you? That's right. What do you think about the things that are happening? This is off my questionnaire, I'm just curious. Oh. You mean to say that? In the South, in the North, whatever. Ah. Well it's a lot of people in both the places that have ways I wouldn't take up with. Mm-hm. Such as? Drinking. Mm-hm. And beating the wives. Mm-hm. Things like that. What do you think of King? Hm? What do you think of Reverend King? And what he's trying to do? What is he trying to do? Oh. Trying in a non-violent way to bring about some kind of justice. Hm. North and South. /?/ Trying to bring about justice. For the Negro. Oh, that's right. /inaudible/ To do that. They have a right to have their rights too. Yeah. Did you- when you were a girl, did you ever hear anything about Marcus Garvey? No. You- you never heard any- any noise about him? When you were young? No. How did you family celebrate the holidays when you were a kid? How would you celebrate Christmas? Well back there they had service Christmas Day. Mm-hm. Were you strong church people? Was your father? Yeah. Very devout /family/? My father was a r- r- I've got mine a- a strict one. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. My father wa- was a strict one when he was living. Mm-hm. What would you do on Christmas morning? Would you say Merry Christmas to each other, or would you say Christmas Gift, or? No, we would just get ready and go on to service, and. Uh-huh. See different friends, I'd know. I'm'a speak to 'em and laugh and go on. Mm-hm. After service. Did you exchange presents, or didn't your father think that this was a fitting way to celebrate? Sometime we'd give one another apples, sometime. Candies and things like that. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Um, did you ever do anything on Halloween? J- you know, the kids make such a big thing /out of it/. I know what you're talking about. But did you ever do anything then? No. Did you get into mischief? No, I didn't do that. Oh. I used to. But, /unintelligible/. That's why you know all about it, cause you got in it. That's right. That's right. Alright then. No, but, uh. But did Halloween mean anything? Did- did you even. Was it a holiday? No, it was fun to me to see them cutting up and playing, and tearing out. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. So you didn't know anything about Halloween until you got here? Or did you in Lou- Louisiana? No. I didn't know anything about it til I come up here. Probably it's still a church holiday in some places. Did- uh, did you and your family ever fight? You and your brothers and sisters? Yeah, we'd fight one another. My step-mother would see us fighting. She'd Uh-huh. come out with a switch. Uh-huh. Make us stop. Uh-huh. Whip both of us. Yeah. Was there any rule for a fair fight? No. Anything's fair, huh? Anything that you started. Uh-huh. Say you were fighting- you had brothers, did you? Yeah, I had m- my mother had ten children. Uh-huh. Who'd you fight with most? A brother or a sister? My brother. Say you were fighting with him and you picked up a brick. No. We wouldn't do that. You wouldn't do that. That wasn't fair. We know that wasn't right. Yeah. People say what you'd do is hit one another and run. Uh-huh. You couldn't kick each other? No, you better not kick me. What would happen if you kicked? Would your parents Yeah. tell you about it? And whip us too. Uh-huh. Okay, um. Have you ever been in a hospital? Me? Yeah. I- I was in the hospital several years ago with my leg. What happened to it? Fell down in the snow. Oh, boy. And tried to get up and couldn't. Yeah. Yeah. Did you break a bone? M- yeah, it broke a bone. That's when I got that stick over there. Mm-hm. How long did they keep you? In the hospital? Hm, I was in there for six- about four week- m- b- a month. Yeah. That's long enough for you to get tired of it, isn't it? /?/ pain started w- Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Before they said I could walk good, I was ready to come out of there. Yeah. Yeah. Sometimes people- have you ever been in a situation where Ooh. you thought you were gonna die? I was then. Okay. Okay. Sometimes people say, whatever's gonna happen is gonna happen. How do you feel about that? Mm, well it went far enough with me with my leg. When it broke, you see it, Mm-hm. the bone shattered. The doctor said, oh, she'll never walk no more. And when I got- kind of got up so I could creep around on it. I close my eyes and told myself, well. I said, well doc. God ain't dead yet. Told him just like that. I said, God n- said. Well, it's alright. I said, God ain't dead yet. What'd he say? Oh, you'll never walk on no hill. Mm-hm. And you'll never walk no more. And you said, just hang on. Yeah. I just, well God ain't dead yet. Ah, that's funny. So you do walk around with your cane? Yeah, I take that stick all over the house with me. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Whittled myself. Mm-hm.
